meta.title: Backpropagation on a tiny network
meta.summary: Forward pass, loss, then gradients flow backward through two layers.

steps.title: Forward: hidden layer
steps.narration: Each hidden neuron sums its weighted inputs: h1 = 1.0*0.4 + 0.5*0.2 = **0.5**, h2 = 1.0*0.3 + 0.5*0.6 = **0.6**.

steps.title: Forward: output
steps.narration: The output combines the hidden values: y = 0.5*0.7 + 0.6*0.5 = **0.65**. The target is 1.0.

steps.title: Loss
steps.narration: Squared error loss L = (1.0 - 0.65)^2 = **0.1225**. The gradient at the output is dL/dy = -0.70, so y should go up.

steps.title: Backward: output weights
steps.narration: Gradients flow backward. dL/dw(h1->y) = dL/dy * h1 = -0.70 * 0.5 = **-0.35**, and for h2 it is **-0.42**.

steps.title: Backward: input weights
steps.narration: The chain rule continues: the error reaching h1 is dL/dy * 0.7 = -0.49. Multiply by each input to get the input-weight gradients.

steps.title: Update weights
steps.narration: Each weight moves against its gradient: w = w - lr * grad. With lr = 0.1, the weight w(h1->y) goes from 0.7 to **0.735**.

scenarios.title: What if the learning rate is too high?

steps.title: Overshoot
steps.narration: With lr = 5 the update is huge: w(h1->y) jumps from 0.7 to 2.45. The next output overshoots the target and the loss gets worse.
